ai.description: This 6–9 cm frog is green with small white or yellow spots. It features a distinct white line along the jaw and outer limbs, with large, fully webbed feet and prominent toe discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Zhangixalus feae* is uniquely distinguished by the presence of prominent, fleshy dermal flaps along the outer edges of its forearms and tarsi, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Zhangixalus feae* inhabits subtropical evergreen forests and moist broadleaf woodlands, typically found at elevations between 800 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Thao whipping frog is primarily nocturnal and arboreal, often congregating around forest pools to breed during the rainy season.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Zhangixalus feae* reproduces via foam nests deposited on vegetation overhanging water. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically laying 100–200 eggs per clutch.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Zhangixalus feae* occurs in Northeast India, specifically in Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, and Mizoram, typically inhabiting montane forests at elevations of 1,000–2,000m.
ai.callDescription: The call of *Zhangixalus feae* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, pulsed chirps, typically heard from vegetation surrounding forest pools or streams.
